title: Diodes That Play With Light Explained Simply | PUC and ISC
description:
Aarav spots a small solar lamp at the college gate. All day it sits in the sun, and at night it lights up by itself. How? Three special diodes that work with light: the light emitting diode (electricity in, light out), the photodiode (light in, signal out) and the solar cell (light in, power out).

A playground slide shows why a light emitting diode glows: electrons slide down the energy gap into holes and give out light. On a live breadboard the diode glows only in forward bias. We derive the colour rule step by step (E = hc/lambda, lambda in nm = 1240 / Eg in eV) and watch the colour move from red to violet as the gap grows. Then a photodiode in reverse bias, with the scope showing the current climb as the light gets brighter, and a solar cell with no battery at all: generation, separation, collection, and its I-V graph in the fourth quadrant. Worked example: the gap of a diode that glows at 620 nm. Then the exam trap, where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 46 of PUC Electronics. Karnataka I PUC Electronics Ch 6: Semiconductors, Diodes and Applications of Diodes | ISC Class 12 Physics: Electronic Devices (special junction diodes: LED, photodiode, solar cell).
